fix_commit_message:
Bug 2013562: Enter correct realm before resolving same-thread waitAsync promise r=arai

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D281314
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 670eb2adbc70 on top of intro 3b5eb00effeb via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (UseAfterFree): js::atomics_notify_impl() implements Atomics.notify(). When it discovers that a waiting Atomics.waitAsync() promise was created on the exact same JSContext as the notifying call (a 'same-thread' notification fast path introduced to avoid dispatching an off-thread task to the event loop), it extracts the PromiseObject and defers resolving it until after the futex/helper-thread locks are released, then calls PromiseObject::resolve(cx, promise, resultMsg) directly in a loop. This loop never enters the promise's realm via AutoRealm before resolving it, even though the promise may belong to a different realm than whatever realm happens to be current on cx (a single JSContext can traverse many realms over its lifetime). Resolving a promise while the wrong realm is entered on the context is a known-dangerous pattern in SpiderMonkey and was fixed by adding an AutoRealm scoped to each promise before calling PromiseObject::resolve. Root cause: The same-thread fast path for Atomics.waitAsync()/Atomics.notify() was added without accounting for the fact that JSContext::realm() can differ from the realm of the promise being resolved; the code assumed 'same context' implied 'same realm', which is not guaranteed in a multi-realm embedding like the browser (e.g. cross-origin iframes, Xray wrappers, or other realm-switching operations happening on the same context).
